description: The one window, and only what a window needs. The shell reaches its own files over frank:// and Studio over fetch; the commands it calls are sync_discover (job 26, 6 Sep) -- the Bonjour browse behind the Sync button -- google_sign_in (job 26b, 6 Sep) -- Google's consent page in the system browser, which Google will not show in a web view -- and audio_session_start (job 8b, 6 Sep) -- which takes the AVAudioSession when the reader first plays, so the audio survives the app switcher; those three through window.TTSTVHost, which lib.rs injects. It takes no argument and can only make this app's own sound keep playing, which is the whole of what a page could do with it. And (G-PULL, 11 Sep) the four book commands -- book_put, book_meta, book_list, book_remove -- through window.TTSTVHost.books: the Cache API refuses frank://, so a book a Sync pulls is written to <app data>/books/ and served back by the frank:// handler; every name they take is checked (a slug, a hash, a path inside the book's folder, refused in words otherwise) and they can reach nothing outside that folder. And (G-SYNCBG, 11 Sep) the three pull commands -- sync_start, sync_status, sync_stop -- through window.TTSTVHost.sync: a Sync's books are downloaded by the app on a thread of its own, so leaving the Settings page no longer cancels them; sync_start takes a job the page built (the books, their files, the Drive token or the LAN pairing), checks every name in it before a byte is fetched, fetches only from Drive's files endpoint or the paired Studio's paths, and writes only through the book door's own functions into <app data>/books/ -- or, for a job of kind language (G-LANG, 11 Sep), through the pack door into <app data>/languages/. And the three pack commands -- dict_langs, dict_lookup, dict_remove -- through window.TTSTVHost.dict: a word looked up in a language pack (one SQLite file per language, opened read-only), the packs on this phone listed, one removed; every name they take is a language code, checked, and they reach nothing outside <app data>/languages/. And (G-LOOKUP2, 13 Sep) the two Apple commands -- lookup_apple and lookup_apple_offered -- through window.TTSTVHost: lookup_apple presents iOS's own UIReferenceLibraryViewController as a half sheet for ONE word, the word the reader pressed, and nothing of Apple's comes back -- none of that panel's text is in this process, so it can only ever be looked at; lookup_apple_offered is a pure question about a language code -- does iOS ship a definition dictionary for it -- asked ONCE per book so the control is never drawn for a Latin or an Ancient Greek book, and it touches nothing at all. There is deliberately no third command: dictionaryHasDefinitionForTerm: costs 31-95 ms a word (23 s for a median chapter, 112 s for a long one), so it is not a door. And (C2/K8, 13 Sep) one read-only command -- inbox_list -- which lists what a share put into this phone: the folders a share extension wrote into the App Group container and the files -- Copy to Frank -- put into <Documents>/Inbox. It takes no argument, reaches nothing outside those two roots, and moves, parses and deletes nothing -- the inbox is where a thing waits. And (G-INBOX, 13 Sep) the two that finish it -- inbox_send and inbox_drop -- through window.TTSTVHost.inbox: send POSTs ONE item's bytes to the paired Studio's own POST /upload (the base and the token are the page's pairing record, and an address that is not http(s) is refused before any fetch); drop removes that one item from one of the two inbox roots, and the page calls it in one place only, after a 200 -- by which time the bytes are on the Mac's drive in TTS_DATA/sources, which is write-once. Every name they take is checked the same way the list checks one (no dot file, no separator, one of the two known roads), so nothing outside the two inbox roots can be reached or removed however a page spells the argument. All three now DO get an init script -- INBOX_JS -- which is also the row on the Library page saying what is waiting and why. And (D1(b), 13 Sep) the seven speech commands -- speech_available, speech_voices, speech_speak, speech_stop, speech_pause, speech_resume and speech_speaking -- through window.TTSTVHost.speech: the phone's own AVSpeechSynthesizer, reading a chapter aloud with no account, no key, no GPU and no network. speech_speak is handed a batch of sentences and QUEUES them on the system synthesiser, which is the whole reason the native door exists: iOS suspends a backgrounded WKWebView's JavaScript, so the D1(a) reader that speaks one sentence and asks the page for the next goes silent the moment the screen locks, and a queued utterance does not. What they take is text, a language code, a voice identifier and three numbers; what comes back is a count, the rate the phone will actually use, and -- four times a second while speaking, by eval and not by a second event bus -- the character range of the word being said, which is what moves the highlight with no timings file anywhere. They can make this app speak its own text and do nothing else: no file is written, nothing is recorded, and no audio leaves the phone. Nothing else beyond core:default is granted. NOTE what is deliberately absent: tauri-plugin-deep-link AND tauri-plugin-opener are registered in lib.rs and get NO permission here, so none of their commands are reachable from the page. Both links a phone receives -- frank-pair:// and Google's redirect -- are read in Rust and written into localStorage from there; a page that could call get_current() could read the pass, or another app's redirect, out of a launch URL, and no page needs to. And opener without a permission cannot be asked to open an arbitrary address: google_sign_in opens Google's authorization endpoint or refuses in words.
